target_customer: Engineering teams that use several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) across laptops and cloud sandboxes
problem: Coding agents do not share what they learned, so teammates' agents repeat investigations and lose context across machines.
business_model: Open source core with a usage-based cloud, priced per million ingested agent-session tokens after a free monthly allowance
product_category: Developer tools, shared memory and messaging for coding agents

founders.name: Shalin Patel
prior_employers: AWS and other engineering teams per YC bio
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: built data infrastructure at Pocus.

founders.name: Deep Utkarsh
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: built GTM agents at Pocus and the AI platform and query compiler at Sigma.

competitors.name: Stash (Fergana Labs)
competitors.what: MIT-licensed, self-hostable shared memory for a team's coding agents that uploads session transcripts
competitors.traction_then: Open source project, usage not stated

competitors.name: Augment Code Cosmos
competitors.what: Shared record of context, outputs and feedback for AI coding teams

competitors.name: MemNexus
competitors.what: Shared team memory across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Cursor

technical_complexity.rationale: Session ingestion, search and agent messaging across clouds are standard infrastructure; retrieval quality on long histories is the hard part, and the site reports BEAM benchmark scores that are company claims.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and self-hostable, with several similar projects and a large vendor entering; stored team histories create some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of late 2026 vendors and open source projects were shipping team memory; no action against OpenCrawl is reported.

market_need_then: Teams running multiple coding agents in 2026 need shared context; many launches of team memory tools in 2026 show demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses getopencrawl.com, a prefix domain, and the GitHub organization getopencrawl.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened
identity.visual_style: Developer tool site with benchmark charts

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repository exists; no press on the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand search found nothing about OpenCrawl; the name overlaps with web crawler products and similar sounding Claw tools in results.

outcome_analysis: OpenCrawl is an active Fall 2026 company with no exit or reported funding. Founders have data infrastructure and GTM agent backgrounds from Pocus and Sigma, but the shared-memory-for-coding-agents space was crowded by mid 2026. Too early for a verdict.
notes: YC page and launch post disagree on the free allowance (200M versus 100M tokens a month); the site says 100M. No funding found in search. Competitor sources are vendor pages and blogs.
